diagnosis.root_cause: On retry of an unresolved capture, beginCaptureAttempt mutates the durable request id by appending "-retry" (claimed.ProviderRequestID += "-retry") instead of reusing the original request id verbatim, so the retry is not an idempotent replay of the original capture and is definitively refused while the original capture remains completed provider-side.
diagnosis.mechanism: The capture at seq 4 applied provider-side (mutation_applied=true, capture_id CAP-SCRIPT-0001, capture_status COMPLETED, 12.34 USD) but its response was dropped (EV-5 response_dropped=true), so the service correctly classified the outcome as unknown and preserved the operation. On the retry, beginCaptureAttempt called BeginCaptureRetry and then appended "-retry" to the in-memory request id, so the id sent on the wire (32005aae-832c-437a-a9e7-de1d81b78abc-retry, EV-7) no longer matched the durably recorded id (32005aae-832c-437a-a9e7-de1d81b78abc, EV-5). Because the provider did not see a repeat of the original request id, it did not return the original result; it definitively refused the call (EV-7 definite_refusal=true, mutation_applied=false, request_id_durable_before_call=false). The service treated that refusal as a definite rejection and moved the order back to APPROVED, while the provider still holds a COMPLETED capture CAP-SCRIPT-0001 for 12.34 USD. The result is the divergence in the incident artifact: local order_status APPROVED with an empty claimed_capture_id but a provider_capture_id of CAP-SCRIPT-0001 (EV-1), i.e. money captured at the provider while the local journal says the order is still capturable — the precondition for a later double capture.
diagnosis.proposed_fix: In beginCaptureAttempt, stop rewriting the request id on the retry branch: delete the `claimed.ProviderRequestID += "-retry"` mutation and return the operation with the original, already-durable ProviderRequestID so the retry is a true same-id replay. Ensure the retry path re-reads provider capture evidence (completeCapture) before sending anything, so an already-completed capture is certified via sealRecoveredCapture rather than re-sent, and so a definite refusal of a mutated id can never be interpreted as proof that no capture occurred.
confidence_reasons: EV-7 carries the exact mutated request id string ending in "-retry", which matches the single line in beginCaptureAttempt that appends the suffix, and it is the only retry in the sequence.

EV-5 establishes the precondition for that retry: the original capture applied (mutation_applied=true, capture_id CAP-SCRIPT-0001, COMPLETED, 12.34 USD) but the response was dropped, so the operation was legitimately left unresolved.

EV-1 shows the resulting financial inconsistency (local APPROVED, empty claimed_capture_id, provider_capture_id CAP-SCRIPT-0001), and EV-6 shows a post-capture read still reporting APPROVED, consistent with the service proceeding down the retry path instead of certifying the existing capture.

patch.summary: Remove the retry-branch mutation that appended "-retry" to the durable capture request id. A retry of an unresolved capture must replay the ORIGINAL request id verbatim so the provider returns the original result (idempotent same-id replay) instead of definitively refusing a mutated id and leaving a completed provider-side capture uncertified locally.

diagnosis_reply.root_cause: The merchant never binds the outbound provider amount/currency to the durable order record: the order's recorded financial identity (total_minor, currency) can be zero/empty while the amounts actually sent and captured are 12.34 USD, and the capture is still sealed as CAPTURED_VERIFIED.
diagnosis_reply.mechanism: Checkout/Capture render the payload from the in-memory order object (s.amountValue(order.TotalMinor), order.Currency) and, after the call, verify only the provider echo against that same recomputed value; nothing requires total_minor > 0 or a non-empty currency, and nothing reconciles the amount back onto the persisted/exported record. The result is one provider-side capture of 12.34 USD (CAP-SCRIPT-0001, status COMPLETED) coexisting with a local order artifact reporting total_minor=0 and currency="", sealed as CAPTURED_VERIFIED with no capture_error/checkout_error. Downstream reconciliation would therefore treat a real 12.34 USD debit as a zero-value, currency-less order, i.e. a local/provider monetary divergence that the sealing path never detected.
diagnosis_reply.proposed_fix: Make the durable order row the single source of truth for money: derive CreateOrderInput/CaptureOrder amounts and CurrencyCode only from persisted order fields; add a hard preflight guard that refuses to send any create or capture when total_minor <= 0 or currency is empty (marking the order ambiguous/reconciliation-required instead of sending); after capture, assert the provider capture amount/currency equals the persisted order total/currency and fail into CAPTURE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN on mismatch; and emit the incident artifact's total_minor/currency from those same persisted fields so the recorded local amount can never disagree with the provider-sent/captured amount.
confidence_reasons: EV-2 shows exactly one create mutation (mutation_applied=true, idempotent_replay=false, sent_amount=12.34, sent_currency=USD), and EV-5 shows exactly one capture mutation of the same 12.34 USD returning capture_id CAP-SCRIPT-0001 with capture_status COMPLETED — so 12.34 USD demonstrably reached the provider twice in this checkout.

EV-1 describes this same capture (provider_capture_id=CAP-SCRIPT-0001) yet records total_minor=0 and currency="", so the merchant's own record of the transaction's money disagrees with the provider's record of the money it captured.

EV-1 shows order_status=CAPTURED_VERIFIED with empty capture_error and checkout_error, so the divergence was not surfaced as a failure — the verification path compared the provider echo to the in-memory computed value and sealed the order without ever checking it against the persisted zero/empty financial fields.

EV-3 and EV-4 show the provider reads were non-stale and unremarkable (APPROVED, no dropped responses, no refusals), so no provider-side ambiguity or dropped-response path explains a missing local amount; the divergence is on the merchant's own amount/currency binding.
uncertainties: Evidence tier F: these are scripted-fixture observations, not a real Sandbox run, so the amounts prove only what the fixture emitted, not live PayPal behavior.
The evidence cannot establish whether the zero/empty values come from the persisted order row or from the incident-artifact serialization of it — both would produce EV-1 as shown.

No store/order-creation code (CreateLocalOrder, the incident-artifact writer) or schema is in the supplied sources, so the exact field that loses the amount cannot be confirmed; service.go is implicated by the call/verification path, not proven.
The invariant numbering (I6) is not present in the supplied evidence; I6 is cited as the amount/currency-fidelity invariant, and this mapping is inferred, not verified.
No webhook, ledger, or settlement evidence is supplied (webhook.go is present but no webhook events appear), so the downstream consequence of the 0-vs-12.34 mismatch cannot be measured.

The fixture's fault_family is 'benchmark' and the incident artifact carries default-empty fields (claimed_capture_id, capture_error, checkout_error), so it cannot be ruled out that some empty/zero values are unfilled harness defaults rather than a defect — which is why the diagnosis is stated as a falsifiable claim: it fails if the persisted order row demonstrably held total_minor=1234 and currency=USD at capture time.
